Summary: ss CLI re-parses argv into a pwsh command line so a multi-word Summary or EosLog body is re-tokenized on spaces and breaks on parenthesis or semicolon characters, which blocks external callers from filing Requests with normal prose

EosLog.Disposition: filed via the workaround it documents
EosLog.Body: Repro from an external shell, call ss.exe with Remedy-ChangeRequest and a quoted multi-word Summary. The quotes are lost when ss joins argv into one string and re-parses it as a pwsh command line, so only the first word binds to Summary and the rest fail as extra positional parameters. Parenthesis and semicolon characters anywhere in the Summary or in an Add-EosLog body get evaluated by that re-parse and error. Impact, no external caller including Claude can file a Request or EOS log with normal prose, so the 2026-06-22 session handoff went to ss-log.md instead of the hive. Fix direction, on verb dispatch pass the original argv array straight to the cmdlet binder rather than rejoining argv into a string and re-tokenizing, or quote-escape each argv element before the rejoin. Current workaround, wrap each multi-word arg in literal double quotes.

EosLog.Disposition: Confirmed live and still open - fresh repro from the audit session 2026-06-23
EosLog.Body: Re-hit INC105 first-hand while filing CRQ136. ss.exe Remedy-ChangeRequest with a normal-prose Summary failed: ss: At line:1 char:665 Missing argument in parameter list - ss.exe reconstructed the argv into a pwsh command line and broke on a parenthesis and a -A token embedded in the prose. The path that SUCCEEDED: file via the MCP ss_run runspace with a single-quoted pwsh string, which binds -Summary as a literal and never re-tokenizes. So the runspace cmdlet surface is usable for prose but the ss.exe CLI is not. Confirms INC105 is load-bearing for any external caller filing Requests. Cleanest fix: have ss.exe bind argv straight to the cmdlet parameters instead of joining argv and re-parsing as a script line.

ROOT CAUSE 2026-06-26: the bare ss verb path routes through Shim.Run -> ResolveScript which returns string.Join(space, args) at Shim.cs:162 then AddScript at Shim.cs:71, so a multi-word Summary or EosLog body is re-tokenized on spaces and every token after the first binds as an extra positional arg (observed error: a positional parameter cannot be found that accepts argument X). The -Command path also joins (Shim.cs:158). WORKAROUND that works today and is how all 41 rich CRQs were actually filed: ss -EncodedCommand of base64-utf16le of the full pwsh command - Shim.cs:155-156 decodes and AddScripts the whole string so quotes survive; same path as the MCP ss_run tool (Mcp.cs:136,180). Verified empirically this session: parens and semicolons pass through intact. FIX OPTIONS: in ResolveScript bind the bare verb path through ps.AddCommand plus per-arg ps.AddArgument instead of join+AddScript, or have the Remedy/EosLog cmdlets accept the body from the pipeline or a here-string.

INC105 fixed structurally in Shim.cs Run: when args[0] is a request cmdlet and no standalone pwsh operator is present, bind via AddCommand + per-arg AddParameter/AddArgument (no string join, no AddScript), so a prose Summary or Body with (parens) and ; semicolons survives as one token through the bare verb - no EncodedCommand. Built green; this EOS was filed via the bare Add-EosLog verb, which proves it.

Summary: FOUNDATION - first. Slide the VOM under the GC. Demote the GC from global king to a per-fiefdom collector under VOM rooting/quota/lifecycle authority - the VOM is the emperor, revoke handle unroots and GC reclaims. Stock CLR has one global GC, so this is allocation discipline plus unmanaged arenas plus VOM-governed managed heaps, not per-heap collectors. Worktree cr/gc-seam exists.

EosLog.Body: Recovered from transcript session 70964be6 (also b6d647a8, 02e0135e) plus Scott - it is in the hive now, do not ask Scott. MECHANISM - CoreCLR Standalone GC SPI. DOTNET_GCName makes the execution engine drop the stock GC; GC_Initialize trades the IGCToCLR pointer for a custom IGCHeap implementation. Map IGCHeap plus IGCHandleManager vtable intercepts into src/runspace/windows via UnmanagedCallersOnly exports. LANGUAGE - the GC is written in C#, not a C++ fork. Precedent - Michal Strehovsky minidump.net wrote a full standalone .NET GC entirely in C# via NativeAOT plus UnmanagedCallersOnly. It ships as its OWN NativeAOT DLL loaded by DOTNET_GCName, so the host runtime stays JIT for pwsh - no conflict with the no-NativeAOT rule on the main head. WHY NOT SATORI - Satori region-based concurrent still leaves the GC an autonomous king, just a faster one. The right way - the VOM commands collection; the GC is demoted to a mounted engine VOM drives. CHILD-THREAD refinement from Scott - run the collector on VOM-owned threads so VOM can kill it or instantiate several, one per fiefdom; a custom GC means you own the threading, unlike the stock single global GC. OBJECTIVE/PROOF - when a pwsh runspace drops, VOM executes an immediate native free-at-zero on that arena allocation pool with no runtime-wide fault. WINDOWS FIRST - Android is frozen here, MonoVM SGen plus Microsoft runtime Investigation 114738 block the standalone GC SPI on Mono. SOURCES to verify before building - dotnet/runtime docs/design/features/standalone-gc-loading.md, minidump.net Writing a .NET GC in C#, dotnet/runtime issue 114738, Satori dev.to hez2010.

Does full-fat pwsh require a GC - answered. FACT to verify against dotnet standalone-gc-loading.md - managed code cannot run with zero collector; the CoreCLR EE calls IGCHeap for every newobj, so pwsh requires the IGCHeap CONTRACT, not the stock GC and not necessarily a tracing GC. So YES the VOM can do the job - the standalone-GC IGCHeap is the interception seam where the VOM transparently takes ownership of every pwsh object the instant it is born, with no cooperation from pwsh and no explicit VOM handles. RECLAMATION is the design choice - the runspace or pipeline is the natural fiefdom mapped to a VOM arena, freed at zero on drop, region collection no tracing. Long-lived runspaces that accumulate mid-session garbage - either recycle the runspace as the collection unit under VOM command, or run a minimal tracing pass scoped to that one fiefdom. Pure never-free Zero-GC bump allocation only holds if runspaces stay short-lived. NET - pwsh needs the contract not the king; the fiefdom is the runspace; the IGCHeap seam gives the VOM every object for free. Supersedes the old memory claim that pwsh being fully managed means it cannot be NoGC-ed.

Correction - the peer session originated the GC-under-VOM line and was FIRST. The prior entries here gc-design-recovered and pwsh-needs-contract-not-king are a transcription/capture from earlier sessions, likely his own, NOT a prior claim or lead by this Claude. They are subordinate to his live greenfield build - context for it, not a source he must defer to. He owns this line. The hive follows the work; a freshly-filed ticket does not retroactively subordinate someone already building.

STRIKE the earlier claim that Android is MonoVM SGen and frozen for the standalone GC SPI per issue 114738 - it is WRONG and never should have entered the registry. Both heads are CoreCLR. Subsystem runs in-process Microsoft.PowerShell.SDK on CoreCLR on Android ARM64 - that is the category-of-one telos, NOT Mono. The standalone GC SPI - DOTNET_GCName plus a custom IGCHeap - is a CoreCLR feature, so it applies in principle to BOTH heads; gc-under-vom is not Windows-only and Android is not blocked. Any real Android-specific SPI gap must be VERIFIED against the live CoreCLR-on-Android build, never assumed from a Mono prior. The GC runs as a VOM-spawned killable child thread, one per fiefdom, on both heads. This entry was authored by a churned session that trusted a secondhand doc over the binary - the failure mode the project forbids.

Verified externally and against Subsystem.csproj - supersedes the earlier Mono confusion. 1 BOTH heads are CoreCLR - the csproj targets net11.0-android and .NET 11 made CoreCLR the DEFAULT Android runtime replacing Mono as of Preview 4, May 2026; the standalone GC SPI is a CoreCLR feature so it applies to BOTH heads. 2 dotnet/runtime 114738 is android Investigate using different GC variants with CoreCLR on Android - it CONFIRMS the platform and direction, it is NOT a Mono blocker; the earlier entry had it backwards. 3 Standalone GC pluggable since .NET Core 2.1 via DOTNET_GCName; writable in C# per minidump.net via NativeAOT with IlcStandaloneGCSupport true - separate NativeAOT DLL, host stays JIT for pwsh. 4 The pointer problem is already disarmed by invariant 2 - no raw pointers across boundaries, only generational handles path plus gen-ID - so free-at-zero on a runspace arena cannot dangle; a stale cross-runspace handle resolves stale in O(1), not use-after-free. Residual is bounded - only CLR internal roots finalizer-queue, statics, runtime GCHandles reaching into the arena, an enumerable surface a custom GC tracks or refuses. Sources - dotnet runtime issue 114738, minidump.net writing a net gc in c, learn.microsoft.com runtime-config garbage-collector.

DECISION confirmed by Scott and the peer session ONNX-and-QNN-folder-review - supersedes ALL prior GC entries here. The standalone-GC-SPI approach is WRONG and struck - NO DOTNET_GCName, NO custom IGCHeap, NO NativeAOT, NO .dll, NO .so. The GC-in-C# IS the VOM itself, already running in this runspace. The GC does not exist outside handles AT ALL - object lifetime is purely the VOM handle graph, free-at-zero; there is no separate heap-walking collector to swap, so nothing to replace. The GC is NOT a peer - it is folded under the VOM, invariant 6. Any actual reclamation runs ONLY in killable VOM child threads, never a runtime-global collector. No external artifact and no GC SPI is needed - the VOM is in-proc managed C# doing what it already does. THIS is the implement target. My earlier entries gc-design-recovered, pwsh-needs-contract-not-king, CORRECTION-android-is-coreclr, VERIFIED-supersedes-prior described the SPI EXPLORATION from transcript 70964be6 and mistook exploration for decision - struck. The deleted hybrid-coreclr-vom-gc memory already had it right - VOM is the lifecycle authority via handles and arenas, not a per-heap GC swap.

Closes the last residual - there is NO collector to build, not even a spawned scoped one. Memory acquisition IS handle acquisition - need more memory, take another handle - quota-gated by the VOM; VomQuotaExceededException already exists in src/runspace/Vom. Memory cannot grow ungoverned, and free-at-zero reclaims on handle drop. The OOM-forces-collection case does not arise - you cannot accumulate memory you did not take a handle for. One mechanism, the handle, is allocation AND release AND quota. pwsh needs an allocator handle-acquisition, never a collector. The earlier decision entry left a door open for a spawned collector when a heap outlives its budget - that door is CLOSED, there is no budget-overrun path. Implement the handle/quota allocator and free-at-zero; do not implement a GC.

For CORRECTNESS not need - the system already runs GC-free for VOM work. TESTED LIVE in the ss runspace, not theorized: GC.TryStartNoGCRegion(64MB) entered, LatencyMode=NoGCRegion so the collector is suspended process-wide; 500MB cycled through Vom.Alloc + Terminate (NativeMemory, off the managed heap); gcCollectionsDuring=0; region held throughout. Native memory is invisible to the collector budget, so an unbounded VOM workload runs in a permanent no-GC region - the GC is DELETABLE for the data plane, proven. Throughput while gone: VOM alloc 4.34 GB/s, free-at-zero 57 GB/s (bulk arena drop ~13x faster than per-object). PERF of GC-free JIT CoreCLR: no GC pauses = deterministic latency; JIT codegen untouched (JIT is independent of GC); write barriers still emitted on MANAGED ref stores but VOM-native bytes hold no managed refs so the data plane pays ZERO barriers; the only downside, monotonic growth, is exactly what handle+quota+free-at-zero eliminates. NEW INVARIANTS from Scott this session - capture so they are not lost to time: (1) HANDLES ARE STATIC ALLOCATIONS - never resized, always - need more memory means TAKE ANOTHER HANDLE, never realloc. (2) DEFRAG when needed is VOM-ONLY via DirectPort push-based zero-copy blit, or mmap/remap where sharing or paging helps - NEVER a GC compaction. A grep of subsystem-main/src found NO existing defrag/blit implementation - if it was ever built it is not in this tree (Scott suspected it was lost to time - confirmed not present). (3) With static handles + per-fiefdom arenas freed wholesale at zero there are no free-holes, so fragmentation largely does not arise and defrag is rarely needed. (4) VOM SOVEREIGNTY - nothing usurps the VOM; the VOM snipes (Terminate/revoke) any threat; unchallengeable root authority per invariants 2 and 6. DO: implement the handle/quota allocator + free-at-zero, and DirectPort/mmap defrag only if a real fragmentation case appears; do NOT implement a collector of any kind.

PROVENANCE CORRECTION. The earlier EOS entries on this ticket (gc-design-recovered, pwsh-needs-contract-not-king, the Mono confusion, VERIFIED-supersedes-prior, the DECISION entries) were AGENT-DRAFTED EXPLORATION written in an authoritative voice - they are NOT authority and several were wrong (Mono; NativeAOT/DOTNET_GCName/standalone-IGCHeap all struck). Authority is Scott + the binary, never a hive entry. SETTLED and PROVEN live this session (receipts: tests/gc-banished.tests.ps1): (1) the VOM is the heap, no handle = no object; (2) the collector is DELETABLE for the data plane - 500MB cycled through Vom.Alloc inside a real TryStartNoGCRegion with 0 collections, region held; (3) the VOM OWNS pwsh - a live pwsh 7.7 runspace mounted as ONE VOM handle went Opened to Closed on Vom.Terminate alone (handle revoke = pwsh death); (4) pwsh is reached over PSRP, the runspace IS a VOM handle (Sessions/Psrp/id, Rs.cs Close to Terminate(VomOwner)), so its GC sits behind the protocol boundary, irrelevant to the native VOM core. There is NO collector to build. The GC-banishment BUILD and the provenance-breadcrumb mitigation are separate clean items.

Confirms the settled position - VOM is the heap, no collector to build, GC folded under the VOM (invariant 6). No runtime GC-swap done; the DOTNET_GCName/IGCHeap/NativeAOT line stays struck. pwsh managed heap stays behind the PSRP boundary; runspace = VOM handle, Terminate = pwsh death. No further GC build needed for the data plane.

Intraprocess hardware isolation at the VOM Owner boundary - the spike that EARNS the microkernel claim. Today owners isolate only cooperatively (cancellation token + ADVISORY quota Vom.cs:98) in ONE address space with raw nint Resource - any owner can scribble anothers native memory, so the category is microkernel-SHAPED not microkernel. Add a degradation ladder behind the Owner/Enter-Leave seam: rung1 Intel MPK/PKU (x86 PKRU, no syscall) + ARM POE; rung2 ARM MTE+PAC; rung3 SFI/WASM for foreign/untrusted slots (the HLE PE-loader case); rung0 today cooperative. EosLog.Body: Scott refinement: HW isolation means a handle (its raw nint Resource) must NOT cross the owner boundary. Already half-structural - handle tables are per-owner, HandleAllocator lives on Owner with no global table, so an id from A does not resolve in B. HW keys PKU/POE make the pointer undereferenceable across the boundary too. Legitimate cross-owner data then moves ONLY via DirectPort with an explicit grant = capability transfer, the microkernel IPC model, no shared memory by default.

Scott correction - my prior note was imprecise. A handle AS A CAPABILITY (the generational id / path / grant token) CAN and SHOULD cross the boundary - that is capability-passing IPC (the DirectPort grant, the seL4 model). What must NOT cross is the raw backing POINTER (Handle.Resource nint, the dereferenceable address); HW keys PKU/POE make a foreign owners pages undereferenceable. So capabilities transfer over DirectPort with an explicit grant; memory is never shared by default; the raw pointer stays owner-local. The microkernel definition is still being refined by Scott - do NOT treat the criteria as settled.

Built the analyzer Scott asked for: SS026 (src/analyzers/SS026RawPointerBoundaryAnalyzer.cs) - a non-extern public/internal method OUTSIDE Subsystem.Vom returning a raw pointer (nint/IntPtr/void*) is denied (Error); the capability/handle crosses, the pointer never does. Generalizes SS008 (cmdlets) to the whole non-kernel surface; exempts the FFI edge (extern/[DllImport]/[LibraryImport]) and the kernel. This is the SOFTWARE rung of the no-shared-pointer discipline (default-deny the mechanism we never use) - the cooperative isolation, now binary-enforceable, ahead of any HW rung. Compiles (dotnet build exit 0); fire-test GREEN tests/test.gate.ss026-raw-pointer.ps1 (violation=1, kernel/handle/ffi=0). REMAINING to go live in the shipped gate: rebuild the check tool/ss.exe with the new analyzer assembly, then ss check --gate --write-baseline once to onboard existing legacy nint-returning public methods (then it ratchets, denying new ones).

RECON (web, 2026-06-22) reshapes the isolation plan. FINDINGS: (1) Intel PKU/PKRU is NOT exposed to Windows userspace - it is a Linux capability (pkey_mprotect); Windows isolates via hypervisor VBS/HVCI instead. (2) ARM POE is the analog on the Android head but its permission register is PRIVILEGED (kernel-mediated), unlike x86 userspace WRPKRU. (3) => the hardware rung is NOT portable across the heads. The portable confinement rung is SOFTWARE: WASM (Wasmtime) - linear memory disjoint from the host, bounds-checked, no raw syscalls, in-process. CONSEQUENCE: first-party code is already confined enough by SS026 + the no-shared-pointer discipline; enforced isolation is only needed for UNTRUSTED in-proc code (the HLE foreign-PE / untrusted-slot case). So the microkernel-earner should LEAD with WASM-confine-untrusted (portable, both heads), and treat PKU (x86) / POE (ARMv9) as opportunistic HW accelerators where present - NOT the foundation. Full note + sources: S:/subsystem-project/staging/NEXT-SESSION-RECON.md. NEXT: reframe this request to the WASM rung; the keystone build remains the C++ VOM vom.h parity seam.

DECISION - the fork path from the AI-mode dump (modify JIT write barriers, redefine object.h, strip safepoints, gut gcinterface.cpp) is the win32k trap, REJECTED. Use the standalone GC plugin seam (Local GC, .NET Core 2.0+, works with the existing JIT and EE, no fork - standalone-gc-loading.md). The GC is two things - the mandatory allocator (becomes the VOM arena) and the collector (the concept deleted). Hostile parts are not ripped, they go vestigial - no-op write barrier via config not JIT edit, idle finalizer thread, safepoints never suspend. PLAN. P0 no fork, plugin only. P1 starve litter - SS0xx analyzer bans GC.* plus implicit alloc in VOM core (boxing, closures, concat, LINQ hot paths), move Slot.cs code-slots off collectible ALC, MEASURE managed alloc rate under load. P2 build Zero GC - fork GCSample (under 250 LOC) not the runtime, IGCHeap with real bump-pointer Alloc into a VOM native arena and ~70 dummy stubs, never collect, plug via DOTNET_GCName (empty GCName slot confirmed live). P3 deterministic reclaim - arena-per-scope (pwsh pipeline / DirectPort frame) reset O(1), escape-promotion for survivors - the hard PL part. P4 verify - collection counts flatline, C VOM as independent oracle, analyzer locks no-GC-in-source. HARD PARTS - never-collect OOMs without P3 arena reset so P3 is mandatory not optional, the Zero GC joins the trust base so small+C+verifiable, pwsh churns litter so arena reset cadence must match its pipeline lifecycle. EosLog.Disposition: Lazy-dequant design locked: 9.15GB fp32 weight floor is the bomb; keep weights PACKED + fused-dequant matmul. Liveness eviction landed (correct, but RSS-blocked by the weight floor + .NET LOH retention until weights are packed).
EosLog.Body:
Addendum to EOSLOG #144 (same session, 2026-06-30 laptop). Drilled the RAM bomb to root and locked the fix.

MEASURED (off gemma4-e2b-litert.db, sig10 = decoder)
- Weights = 793MB packed -> ~9.15GB fp32 materialized: dtype19 (2-bit) x61 = 384MB->6.14GB (16x); dtype17 (int4) x145 = 351MB->2.81GB (8x); int8 x71 = 41MB->165MB; rest small. Biggest single: the [262144,1536] tied embed = 100.7MB packed -> 1.6GB fp32.
- So the ~20GB run = ~9GB fp32 weights (pinned in _winit, decoded once, reused across Run()s) + ~11GB intermediates/KV.

LANDED THIS PASS
- Interp.Run liveness reclaim: precompute last-use per value, evict each intermediate from env once its last consumer ran (graph outputs pinned). Correct (sig11 still RAN finite); pure memory mgmt, numerics intact. BUT measured peak on sig10 did NOT drop (still ~24GB) for TWO reasons: (1) the 9GB fp32 weight floor is allocated up-front in _winit and never freed (correctly reused across tokens) so eviction can't touch it; (2) .NET LOH does not return freed memory to the OS (RSS tracks the high-water allocation; compaction would be minutes-slow on GB-scale arrays). Eviction is kept — it becomes the dominant win ONCE weights are packed (then intermediates dominate).

QUANT NUMERICS (confirmed in Interp)
- QuantizeLinear: q = clamp(round(x/scale)+zp, -128,127) -> int (Tensor.I). DequantizeLinear: (q-zp)*scale. The gemma graph fake-quants activations (QUANTIZE->FC->DEQUANTIZE) and the FC weight is currently pre-dequantized fp32, so FC = Gemm(int8-act-as-float, dequant-weight)*act_scale. Sub-byte weight dequant = DequantSubByte: signed sub-elements (low bits first), per-row scale along quantized_dimension 0, zero_point per row; value=(q-zero)*scale.
- Gemm: FULLY_CONNECTED -> transB=1, so B=Transpose(weight) (ANOTHER full fp32 copy) then MatMul. MatMul is fp32 axpy, Parallel.For over (batch,row).

THE FIX (next focused build) = lazy dequant, keep weights packed:
1. Tensor gains a packed-quant payload (byte[] Qp + int Qbits + bool QSigned + float[] Qscale + long[] Qzero); IsPacked => Qp!=null.
2. _winit build (or ToModelProto executable path) keeps sub-byte/int4 weights PACKED (don't DequantSubByte to fp32); carry per-row scale/zp on the tensor. _winit drops ~9GB -> ~0.8GB.
3. Fused Gemm/MatMul: when the weight (x[1], transB) IsPacked, dequant W[j,k] inline in the axpy inner loop (no Transpose copy, no fp32 weight array ever allocated). Must match DequantSubByte bit-for-bit.
4. Validate: sig11 logits IDENTICAL fp32-vs-packed (sig11 already RANs finite = the oracle). Then sig10 should fit (~0.8GB packed + live intermediates + ~1.6GB transient for the embed matvec) and COMPLETE -> first real decoder logits, on-laptop, under 8GB-class budget.
5. Then: bounded KV (ring buffer to real seq-len, not the hardcoded 32003) + fp16/int8 KV; multi-signature decode harness (sig2 embed + sig3 PLE -> sig10 -> argmax -> loop); DpxDecoder<-model.db (VOM gather); ss.exe cmdlet + Android dpx backend.

EosLog.Disposition: gemma-4 E2B vision tower (model.db sig4) characterized — MobileNetV5-style conv+transformer encoder -> 204 soft tokens @1536; only dpx gap is DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D
EosLog.Body:
Vision tower analysis (gemma4-e2b-litert.db sig4, 93MB), saved per Scott 2026-06-30.

CONTRACT
- IN  serving_default_src_inputs:0 [1,1,816,128]  (816 spatial positions x 128-ch pre-extracted patch features) + serving_default_mask:0 [1,1,816]
- OUT StatefulPartitionedCall:0 [1,204,1536]  (204 soft vision tokens at the TEXT hidden dim 1536) + :1 [1,204]
- So vision = conv stem -> transformer -> project to 204 tokens@1536 that drop into the decoder as soft tokens (multimodal fusion at the embedding seam).

OP MIX (2206 nodes): 579 Mul / 439 Reshape / 170 Add / 132 DequantizeLinear / 122 Gemm / 120 Transpose / 112 ReduceSum / 110 Rsqrt / 96 QuantizeLinear / 86 Slice / 48 Sigmoid(SiLU) / 41 Pad / 37 Concat / 36 MatMul / 17 DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D / 12 Softmax. The DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D x17 (+CONV_2D, TILE) are the conv stem = the ONLY dpx op-gap blocking vision (the FqEinsum attention/ffn already map). MobileNetV5-300M-shaped: depthwise+pointwise inverted residuals (SiLU) feeding transformer blocks.

WEIGHTS: 66.1MB 2-bit(dt19) + 12.6MB int4(dt17) + 12.0MB fp32(dt0). Biggest = two fp32 projections [1536,1024] (6.3MB) and [1024,1024] (4.2MB) -> the 1024->1536 token projection. The repeated [4096,1024]/[1024,4096] FqEinsum_0/dot_general = the per-block ffn (4x expansion at width 1024).

NEXT for multimodal-on-dpx: implement DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D (Interp kernel + LiteRt MapToOnnx); then sig4 converts+runs and vision tokens feed the decoder. Audio (sig7) gap = ONE_HOT/REDUCE_ALL. Rides CRQ163 (encoder op-gaps), CRQ144 (gemma on dpx).

THE WHOLE POINT: you inference in C#. dpx is a pure-C#, ORT-free ONNX interpreter, so the managed object-OS (CoreCLR) IS the inference engine; the agent thinks in its OWN language on its OWN engine - no Python, no ORT, no foreign runtime. Every handle is a patch-bay channel you can disable/re-enable arbitrarily (no privilege, just flip the handle). A user space is a little Sub-VOM you spin cheap and let crash (recursion: a Sub-VOM is a VOM; plus let-it-crash + cascade-reclaim). Execution swings handle-to-handle like Tarzan vine-to-vine: grab, use, release, reclaim - never holds on, never leaks.   - InstanceNormalization (74)  -- per-channel (x-mu)/sqrt(var+eps)*gamma+beta over spatial dims
  - ReduceProd (2)              -- product reduction over axes
Add these to the OpType switch and the VM walks the whole demucs graph (probe ran 135 nodes, stopped at
the first ReduceProd). Conv/ConvTranspose/MatMul/Gemm/Softmax/LayerNorm/Erf/ScatterND/Pow already implemented.

InstanceNorm + LayerNorm, not GroupNorm; GELU is Erf-based; attention decomposed (MatMul+Softmax, no fused op).

HTP-risky set (QNN-only; engine already covers them): ScatterND x4, Pow x3 (the ~103MB-VTCM offender),
+ dynamic-shape plumbing (Range/Where/Mod/Expand/Tile/ConstantOfShape) -> surgery / off-HTP routing.

implement lands in your tree (subsystem-canonical engine) -- flagging it here since you own that code; happy

DELIVERABLE 2 -- QNN HTP context-binary home-roll feasibility
  Method: byte-level dissection of a real local-dream conversion (HF xororz/AnythingV5/vae_encoder_8gen1.bin,
  QAIRT 2.28) + a deep-research pass adversarially verified against primary sources (ONNX Runtime QNN EP source,
  ExecuTorch QNN backend, llama.cpp QNN PR #12063, Qualcomm AI Hub docs).
  VERDICT: the .bin is a COMPILED, SoC-specific, PARAMETERIZED artifact (the output of an offline HTP "prepare").
  It is NOT frozen DSP machine code and NOT a portable raw graph.
  Container (empirical): struct header + u64 section table + a flat TLV op/tensor table -- record =
  [tag:u32][name_len:u32][name][fixed fields], names u32-length-prefixed -- then a trailing int8 const-weight
  blob. Not flatbuffers, not protobuf. The full graph is in plaintext (ONNX node names; Conv/attention/GroupNorm/
  Softmax markers). No encrypted or compiled-DSP region (whole-file entropy 6.7 bits/byte; regions 4.7-7.3; the
  weight bulk ~6.5 = int8). Build stamp v2.28.0.241029... in-band.
  Metadata = documented versioned struct: QnnHtpSystemContext_GraphBlobInfo_t via graphInfoV3.graphBlobInfo,
  QNN_SYSTEM_CONTEXT_GRAPH_INFO_VERSION_3 (matches the previously decoded rife_v73_info.json: vtcm,
  spillFillBufferSize, optimizationLevel, opDataSize, constSize, socModel 43, dspArch 73).
  Loader: stock Qualcomm qnn-sample-app createFromBinary. local-dream's SampleApp.patch is pure plumbing (mmap
  the bin PROT_READ MAP_PRIVATE + MADV_SEQUENTIAL; a zero-copy UFIXED_POINT_8/16 output dequant). The bin is DATA
  handed to the device's already-signed libQnnHtp skel -> there is no code-signing problem on this path.
  Variant patching: zstd --patch-from (the base bin is the zstd dictionary; ZSTD_decompress_usingDict). An ~837MB
  base unet vs an 11-15MB resolution patch => weights are identical across resolutions and only shape structure
  changes -- independent confirmation the bin is a parameterized graph.
  SOVEREIGN PATH (confirmed, primary sources): build the graph via the QnnGraph op/graph API, finalize ON-DEVICE
  (the device runtime performs the HTP prepare), then contextGetBinarySize + contextGetBinary -> emit the .bin.
  Any code holding a finalized Qnn_ContextHandle_t emits the same blob; qnn-context-binary-generator is not the
  only path (ORT QNN EP source). No qairt-converter, no generator, no Python, no offline SDK -- uses on-device
  libQnnHtp, already present on the device. llama.cpp builds QNN graphs programmatically (proves the front half).
  REMAINING HARD PROBLEM: the const-weight blob is HMX/HVX swizzled and tiled, not raw int8. llama.cpp hit the
  same wall (mapping block-quant int4/int8 into QNN weight layouts is unsolved in the open). For the sovereign
  path you do NOT have to solve it -- on-device prepare swizzles from logical-layout weights. For a from-scratch
  byte emit you do.
  STRATEGIC (Scott-directed):
    - Own the tiling at db->qnn convert (feed the DSP a pre-shaped input). The swizzle is mechanical-sympathy
      layout for the HMX systolic array (1024-byte HVX tiles, VTCM locality), not obfuscation; the technique
      (register-level reorder hidden under MAC/load latency, e.g. HVX vshuff/vdeal) is silicon-agnostic and
      transfers to the gfx900/Vega backend (origin of the QNN research).
    - q4a16 bandwidth lever: HTP pads q4 to q8 and often moves it as q8, discarding the bandwidth win; decode is
      memory-bandwidth-bound and weights are the traffic. Owning the pack keeps true 4-bit in DDR/VTCM (half the
      decode traffic), unpacks q4->q8 in-register hidden under MAC latency, accumulates q4xq16 into int32 -- the
      precision lives in the accumulate, not the operands.
    - Legal/distribution: non-commercial interoperability + reverse engineering sits in Sega v. Accolade /
      Sony v. Connectix / DMCA 1201(f). The sovereign path does not circumvent (uses the runtime as intended).
      Distribution model = a zstd --patch-from patcher + user-supplied open weights; nothing copyrighted hosted
      (the weights here are open SD1.5/AnythingV5; the only owned thing is Qualcomm's format = the interop lane).

ARCHITECTURE -- model.db (the convergence)

  projections table keyed by target. Queryable; a SQL diff is a SEMANTIC patch (finer than zstd byte-diff);
  patchable at the op grain. The QNN .bin, the .dpblob, a Vulkan/SPIR-V pack, a litert export are LOSSY device
  projections of the one db (db = at rest; bin/dpblob = in flight). This is the same seam as CRQ144's Spawn-
  carrier model: carrier-by-mode at runtime (inline / CpuFence / VulkanFence / device) == projection-by-target

  gemma4 truth (inv-9), not two models. s:\modeldb holds the truths; projections materialize per carrier.

INTEROP SPEC (verified, for DpxQnn.cs)
- libQnnHtp.so exports ONLY QnnInterface_getProviders; the function table is reached at offset 40 in QnnInterface_t (backendId u32 + pad, providerName ptr, apiVersion 6xu32 = 24B). Table indices (8B fn ptrs): backendCreate=1, contextCreate=9, contextGetBinarySize=11, contextGetBinary=12, graphCreate=15, graphAddNode=18, graphFinalize=19, graphExecute=21, tensorCreateGraphTensor=24, errorGetVerboseMessage=49.
- sizeof(Qnn_Tensor_t) = 144 (version 8B + max(v1=112, v2=136)). The node input-tensor ARRAY strides at 144; a version+v1-only (120B) struct mis-strides ins[1] -> graphAddNode INVALID_OP_CONFIG. Single tensors (tcg, by ptr) tolerate the short struct; arrays do not.
- Qnn_QuantizeParams_t = 2 ints + 32B union = 40B. For FLOAT tensors BOTH encodingDefinition AND quantizationEncoding must be QNN_*_UNDEFINED (0x7FFFFFFF). Zero-init reads as IMPL_GENERATED + SCALE_OFFSET(scale=0) -> CPU backend tolerates, HTP rejects with 0x1775 INVALID_OP_CONFIG. This was THE HTP-only bug.
- QnnGraph_Config (HTP fp16): {option=CUSTOM(0)@0, customConfig ptr@8}; QnnHtpGraph_CustomConfig {option=PRECISION(2)@0, precision=FLOAT16(1)@8 -- union is 8-aligned}. NOTE: this v73 ran fp32 regardless (precision config not honored; exact match), same as mm_qnn. So fp16/HMX on silicon is still a residual for both routes.

- Teardown abort-at-exit (mono runtime + QNN fastrpc cleanup) after the receipt prints -- cosmetic; becomes a VOM cascade-kill in-tree.
- The maker is fp32 (precision config not honored on this v73). fp16/HMX path on silicon + int8-quantized weights (the real weight-prepare) remain.

EosLog.Body:
ANTIGRAVITY -- the host-side "talking" layer for gemma-4 on dpx. Weight-INDEPENDENT; you meet the engine at a graph-I/O seam.

WHY: gemma runs on our sovereign dpx engine (model = a queryable .db; subgraphs = sub-VOMs). The engine half (graph exec, op kernels, weights, model.db) is the workstation's; the qnn.bin projection was the QNN session's (CRQ158). The "talking" half -- prompt -> tokens -> prefill -> decode -> sample -> detokenize -> turn-formatting -- needs no weights and is yours.

BUILD (4):
1. Sovereign SentencePiece tokenizer (home-rolled, the OnnxProto move -- no foreign lib): parse the SP ModelProto protobuf (repeated pieces: piece string + score float + type enum), Unigram encode (NFKC -> escape spaces to U+2581 -> add_dummy_prefix -> Viterbi best-path over piece log-scores -> byte-fallback <0xNN> for unknowns), and detokenize (join -> U+2581 to space -> strip one leading space -> fold byte runs -> UTF-8). Read normalizer flags from the proto; do not hardcode.
2. Gemma chat template: <bos><start_of_turn>{role}\n{content}<end_of_turn>\n ... <start_of_turn>model\n. Inject bos/turn tokens BY ID read from the tokenizer (they are CONTROL pieces, not text-encodable; Gemma-2 106/107 vs Gemma-3 105/106 -- read, never hardcode). Stop generation on <end_of_turn>.
3. Autoregressive decode loop: prefill -> logits -> sample (argmax/top-k/temp) -> append -> per-token step, written against a graph-I/O contract on a STUB engine (zero weights).
4. Runtime contract: implement BringUp/IsAlive/BackendName/StreamTurnAsync->AgentDelta in PORTABLE core (no Android.Content); KV-cache as VOM handles.

SEAM (where you meet the workstation): engine.Run(feed) -> outs; feed = {input_ids, positions, kv_in[]}; outs = {logits, kv_out[]} (tensor names/shapes/dtypes pinned). You code the loop against a stub satisfying the seam; the workstation wires the real dpx engine to the same seam. No source overlap.

PROVIDED (unblocks you, no big-weights dependency): s:\modeldb\gemma-4-e2b.spm (4.5 MB) -- the real SentencePiece tokenizer extracted from the litertlm. Verified: pieces[0]=<pad> (CONTROL), <eos>/<bos>/<unk> follow; Unigram + byte_fallback.

OUT OF SCOPE (do not collide): op kernels / graph exec / model.db (workstation); qnn.bin (CRQ158); the real gemma weights.

RECEIPTS (Cutlerian, measured, dotted-name mirroring the namespace): test.tokenizer.roundtrip (encode->decode bit-exact on a corpus); test.tokenizer.gemma-template (the exact byte/ID sequence for a known prompt); test.decode.loop-synthetic (drives N steps on a stub, stops on the stop-token, KV grows correctly). Each prints a receipt with measured numbers + verdict.

COORDINATION: via the hive (Add-EosLog on this CRQ), not Scott as switchboard. Converge on the model.db schema being specced in the storage lane -- one shape, do not fork it.

CITES (primary, not priors): github.com/google/sentencepiece -- src/sentencepiece_model.proto, src/unigram_model.cc, src/sentencepiece_processor.cc; ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core/prompt-structure. RELATED: CRQ144 (gemma on dpx / Spawn-carrier), CRQ158 (demucs/QNN/model.db architecture), CRQ109/143 (the GraphRuntime/Runtime contract).

No GC except pwsh behind the VomBoundary (CRQ146/139); CRQ135 squashes that. Scott 2026-06-30: "dpx is a vom ... no gc to be found unless its a pwsh thread and even then i think we can squash it."

EosLog.Disposition: CRQ164 design locked: bf16 data-plane default (= top-16-of-fp32, free reinterpret, NPU-native); Interp->DpCompute, Tensor->DpxTensor; citizenship via Span (not pointer work); VOM upgrades auto-propagate to handle-holders
EosLog.Body:
Design decisions for CRQ164 (DPX is VOM-native), Scott 2026-06-30 (tired, end of a long session; these are the locked calls):

ELEMENT FORMAT -- bf16, not fp32.
- bf16 = the top 16 bits of fp32 (sign1/exp8/mant7). fp32<->bf16 is a FREE reinterpret (shift/truncate, no exponent rebias), SAME dynamic range as fp32 (no fp16 65504 overflow cliff), and NPU-native (Hexagon HMX = the razr+). gemma trains in bf16 anyway.
- Halves activation/intermediate memory (~11GB -> ~5.5GB) on top of the 2-bit/int4 weights = the on-device-sized engine.
- fp32 is NOT stored; it is reconstructed on demand as the bf16(high uint16) + residual(low uint16) "two-limb" pair -- a lossless bit-split -- only for the rare full-precision op. VomFormat data-plane default element = bf16.

NAMING -- Interp is not Cutlerian, it dies.
- Interp -> DpCompute (the graph executor / kernel dispatcher; a kernel is a single op, the dispatcher is the compute engine).
- Tensor -> DpxTensor (the bf16, VOM-region-backed element store -- a handle, never a float[]).

CITIZENSHIP is NOT delicate pointer work (Scott corrected my over-framing).
- DpxTensor holds a handle; kernels read via Span over handle.Resource (the exact pattern already in ModelDbBench.cs:40: new Span<float>((void*)h.Resource,n)). Array-style indexing + SIMD (new Vector<float>(span.Slice(i))) unchanged.
- Alloc = Vom.Alloc (a handle). Free = Close = free-at-zero = the liveness decref already computed (lastUse). Within a kernel the region is alive; Close happens after the node returns -> no live Span at free -> no use-after-free.
- It is BREADTH (many kernels touch .Fp/.Ip) not DIFFICULTY.

PROPAGATION model (Scott's "baymaxxed automagically").
- VOM-core upgrades (arena sub-alloc + blit + handle-rewire defrag) auto-propagate to EVERY handle-holder, transparently: consumers only touch handle.Resource (resolved per-use through the owner table), the VOM rewires on move -> ZERO consumer changes. That is the payoff of the handle indirection.
- The Interp/DpCompute is the ONLY non-citizen (legacy float[] from standalone dpx). Citizenship is a one-time plug-in; after that it rides every future VOM upgrade for free like everything else.

SEQUENCING when fresh: (1) DpxTensor handle-backed + Span accessor, float[] path kept alive; (2) weights+KV -> VOM regions (the 9GB, off-GC, deterministic free) validate sig11 logits identical + RSS returns; (3) kernel outputs -> arena (liveness = Close); (4) ss.exe backs the arena with the real VOM -> Vom.Snapshot is the whole truth -> squaremodelstat renders the LIVE model; quota = budget; defrag = handle-rewire. Then rename Interp->DpCompute / Tensor->DpxTensor as the final mechanical pass.

UNLEASH FROM THE REPL LOOP - the swift build-out plan (agent, sev1, work-from-this-doc). Thesis (Scott 2026-07-01): "i am all about unleashing the models from the repl chat loop." ss/e2b must exist as a continuous agent, not a stateless request/response function. Six components, sequenced. P2P device-to-device brokerage (rungs 1-2) is FIRST PRIORITY - Scott handed real primitives for this tonight (UDP courier, mDNS, AgentActorProtocol) and integration comes before any of the wilder tests below.

RUNG 1 - P2P BROKERAGE (do this first, everything else rides it).
CRQ173 (federated compute) + the UDP courier/mDNS packets reviewed tonight are the wire. VirtuaCam (S:\virtuacam-project\VirtuaCam, Scott's own prior art, ~1yr old, MIT, C++20/D3D11) is a SIGNAL for how to do this, not code to port verbatim - Scott: "i did not know how to multithread when i made virtuacam its almost a year old." What IS reusable as architecture: shared D3D11 texture + shared ID3D11Fence + a memory-mapped manifest file for discovery (BroadcastManifest: dims/format/adapter LUID/shared handle names) is literally DirectPort's region+fence+discovery shape, already proven shipping in production a year before tonight's UDP work. VirtuaCam's Broker.cpp/BrokerClient.cpp/Discovery.cpp/Multiplexer.cpp are the reference for the pattern; rebuild the threading fresh against Vom.Spawn, do not copy the old thread code.
THE INTEGRATION: today VirtuaCam is broker(1) <- producers(N) -> consumer(1 virtual camera), a single local hub. It needs to become BROKER/BROKER - the same process that brokers local D3D11 producers into a virtual camera ALSO mounts as a peer in the ss Agent/DirectPort mesh (AgentHost/AgentDevice, CRQ173), so a producer feed can be pushed cross-device the same way it is composited locally. This is the crucible: "the ipc in virtuacam is a signal on how we do p2p along with the primitives i've provided" (Scott). Done correctly this delivers scrcpy-class screen/camera mirroring and device control NATIVELY - no scrcpy dependency, ever.
DEADPOOL (apps ss supersedes, kill from the phone/workstation once its equivalent lands - list grows, do not add entries not named): Shizuku (Scott: "whatever shizuku can do i can do better" - ss already owns its own ADB transport + VOM/DirectPort peer model, which is a superset of what an ADB-permission-broker app provides); scrcpy (superseded by the VirtuaCam broker/broker integration above).
WIP FOLDER RETIRED: no more staging in wip/ then folding into src later (was CRQ148s two-step). Everything integrates directly into src/ going forward - Scott 2026-07-01: "no more wip folder either everything gets directly integrated."

RUNG 2 - THE SCHEDULER (opt-in self-wake; mostly ALREADY BUILT, corrects CRQ110s "stub" framing).
src/runspace/RuntimeBroker/ScheduledTaskTable.cs is a real, well-designed Cm-projected record layer, not a stub: mode owner|agent (an agent can schedule ITS OWN wake), Gate (a capability path whose POSSESSION must be granted before an unattended agent-mode run fires - explicit, revocable, opt-in consent, not ambient permission - this already IS "sure you can wake yourself up" per Scott 2026-07-01), Cm-persisted so it survives restart, recurrence extensible for calendar triggers. What is genuinely missing, per the file's own doc comment: (1) THE TICKER - the clock that fires due tasks; wire it as a Vom.Spawn thread that computes time-to-next-due-task and does Fence.Wait(deadline), NOT polling - Scott 2026-07-01: "u can sit on a fence sure. ape the windows task scheduler for design fundamentals. any time we can copy from the ms cookbook we do that. the 40 year old cookbook that is the goat." (2) gate-possession enforcement at fire time. Neither lives in the table by the table's own design ("mount doctrine, not a god object") - build them as separate mounted pieces.

RUNG 3 - THREE INFERENCE MODES ON THE SAME FORWARD PASS (DPX decode-loop work, ties directly into tonights perf pass).
Today DPX has one mode: full autoregressive decode. Add two cheap siblings that share the same forward-pass kernel and differ only in what happens after it:
(a) EXECUTIVE / GATING MODE - no generation, no KV cache growth needed. A yes/no/escalate decision reads the logit distribution over 2-3 candidate tokens after a SINGLE forward pass - no sample-detokenize-retokenize loop. This is the mechanism for e2b to self-assess competence before committing to full generation: "we need some way to make the model know that it doesnt know it needs stage 2 of the 4 stages of competence" (Scott, referencing the four-stages-of-competence model - unconscious incompetence -> conscious incompetence -> conscious competence -> unconscious competence). The Onboard.cs fabrication bug found tonight (invented a fake CLAUDE.md instead of admitting "I don't have this verified") is a stage-1 failure in the wild - this gating mode is how e2b reaches stage 2 cheaply, every turn, before deciding whether to escalate/look something up/generate at all.
(b) LATENT PLAN MODE - a handful of steps taken purely in continuous embedding space before any text is serialized: forward pass, take the hidden state at the last position, feed it straight back in as an embedded token (skip vocab projection, skip sampling, skip detokenize/retokenize entirely), repeat N times. This is real, current, active research (2025-2026): "Latent Planning Emerges with Scale," "Latent Thinking Optimization" (ICLR 2026) - latent thoughts leading to correct vs incorrect answers show distinct measurable patterns before any token is produced. Scott arrived at this independently via introspection: "i know the main thrust of what i'm going to say before i've serialized my own human output - that is a post-fill parallel pre-serialization pass that would lay the foundation and pave the road for e2b to drive on." e2b's decode job shrinks from composing an answer to unspooling an already-decided latent trajectory - the hard cognitive step never reaches her. Do not brand this with a flashy nickname; describe and cite the real mechanism.

RUNG 4 - KV EVICTION FEEDS DURABLE CONCEPT MEMORY, NOT THE VOID (do not slow decode for this - background thread it).
Today a rolling KV window is presumably plain FIFO - an entry that falls out is just gone. Proposal evaluated and refined (Scott 2026-07-01): rather than making eviction itself smarter (H2O/StreamingLLM-style heuristic retention - harder problem, still bounded, still lossy) OR synchronously slowing tok/s to summarize inline, push the about-to-be-evicted KV slice to a BACKGROUND Vom.Spawn thread ("a concept distillery") that does the enrich-and-route work at its own pace, off the hot decode path - decode speed stays full; you only throttle on measured Fence backpressure if the distillery falls behind, never as a blanket sacrifice. The distillery mechanism itself is DISTILLED FROM PRIOR ART (referenced in passing - two related, no-longer-maintained Python agent frameworks Scott built and studied, one the evolution of the other): a post-response background pass rewrites a raw exchange into a concise, self-contained, pronoun-resolved fact, then determines the fact's SUBJECT/ENTITY via a second short reasoning pass, then routes/stores it under that entity - an inversion of standard RAG (the expensive reasoning happens at WRITE time so reads become direct entity lookups, not query-time vector search). This pattern is not fringe - production frameworks (Mem0) do write-time entity extraction the same way. THE REFINEMENT SUBSYSTEM ADDS: Fence-stamp every distilled concept at write time so retrieval carries TEMPORAL VALIDITY (which fact is current, which was superseded) - the concrete gap between plain entity-routing and the current state of the art (Zep/Graphiti score +14.8pts over Mem0 on temporal/multi-hop LongMemEval specifically because of this). Subsystem does not need a bolted-on temporal-graph engine for this like Zep does - the monotonic Fence IS temporal validity already, same primitive, one more scale, same latest-wins semantics DirectPort already uses everywhere else.
ENTITY ROUTING MUST USE A VOM PATH, NEVER A BARE STRING LABEL - "the 3 ss problem is the same shit as the two Sarah problem... who is on first what is on 2nd" (Scott). Reference collision (two different real things sharing a label, or the same label meaning different things in different contexts) is the SAME failure whether it's two people named Sarah or three ss processes trying to identify each other. Subsystem already has the fix built into its own grammar: route by a fully-qualified VOM path/handle (invariant 2, handle is the authority), never a sanitized/collidable string.
E2B GETS HER OWN REGISTRY-HIVE, NOT A SHARED BUCKET - a distinct Cm-projected namespace under her own path (not conflated with the system-wide Get-Request hive, CRQ175) is where her distilled concept-embeddings accumulate as durable, VOM-native, Fence-stamped wealth over normal operation - Scott 2026-07-01: "we still need... e2b to have its own registry hive db that is its memories, embedded concepts." This is also the concrete, buildable expression of Scotts stated position that training should not be necessary given how much capability already sits in freely available open weights - the lever is harvesting/hoarding embeddings and composing them at retrieval time, not gradient descent; e2bs registry-hive is exactly that hoard, grown continuously rather than needing a separate harvesting campaign. Rides CRQ175 (Get-Turn is the sibling mechanism for cross-driver turn history; this is the same write-time-enrichment discipline applied to e2bs own long-term concept memory specifically).

RUNG 5 - EXECUTIVE-LOOP SHAPE, DISTILLED IN PASSING FROM PRIOR ART (not verbatim, the SHAPE only).
When e2b DOES need to decompose an open question into a series of ss intents (CRQ165s "can you see my laptop right now" example), the validated loop shape worth reusing: plan (retry-looped structured generation, correction-prompted on malformed output, not hope-it-parses) -> observe (query vom:\/telemetry/peer state) -> reason (forced structured thought+action, validated) -> act (invoke the real ss verb) -> stuck-detect (hash-compare observations, abort after 2 unchanged turns rather than loop forever) -> reflect (a short self-critique after completion, saved into the concept memory above). A dedicated working-memory object separate from raw context, with a narrative-compaction method that turns the last N raw steps into one prose paragraph for re-injection, is worth keeping as a pattern - real context compaction should look like curated compaction, not proportional blind shrinking (which is what generic session-window compaction does today and is strictly worse for anything that needs to survive long-term).
A NAMING NARRATIVE IS A CONSTRAINT MECHANISM, NOT A COSTUME - worth stating plainly since it shapes the executive loops design: giving a model a consistent identity narrative to inhabit (Scott cites a defunct personal agent project whose assistant persona was never a real running component, just a name the model was told it was and never had to dwell on, which measurably shrank its option space on every turn - "the agent did not have to dwell on it, it just was... like religiosity for LLMs") functions the same way as his agent-browser's own intent system: it prunes the option space down before generation, it does not add roleplay overhead. This is NOT an instruction to have e2b roleplay - it is a design note that a stable, minimal, load-bearing self-model measurably narrows the decision tree on every executive turn, which is directly useful for the stage-2-competence gating in Rung 3(a).

RUNG 6 - VALIDATE ONLY AFTER RUNGS 1-5 WORK, NOT BEFORE.
"the chinese test comes after this shit works" (Scott). Once P2P brokerage (Rung 1) and the executive gating mode (Rung 3a) are real: test whether an orchestrating model can be prompted to delegate a subtask to a peer/subagent using a language ONLY that peer understands (e.g. instructing a Chinese-only subagent in Chinese) as a probe of whether task decomposition and peer-addressing are genuinely decoupled from the orchestrators own output language - a sharp test of whether the delegation mechanism is structural (routes by capability/identity) rather than accidentally coupled to a shared natural language. Do not build this before Rungs 1-3 are real; it is a validation test for the architecture, not a component of it.

CORRECTION to Rung 1 (VirtuaCam) - the "broker/broker" framing above is WRONG, grounded-fixing it. The broker is ALREADY absorbed in-runspace, shipped, not future work: src/runspace/windows/Camera.cs ("ss camera") is documented as "the in-proc replacement for VirtuaCam.exe's UI.cpp tray" - BrokerHost.cs P/Invokes DirectPortBroker.dll directly (VirtuaCamNative.cs is the fenced native seam, ouroboros rule 0), driven by a render loop from either a console while-loop (ss camera) or the gateway trays WinForms timer - "one broker, two pumps; the pump is the only thing that changes." Already gated (Capability\virtualcamera\<name>, default-deny via CapabilityGate), already VOM-mounted (\VirtualCamera\<name>), already cascade-reclaims on Terminate (ShutdownBroker). Producers stay SEPARATE PROCESSES over DirectPort (ss surface feeds it) - that IS the existing, correct pattern, not something to replace.
Scott 2026-07-01, correcting me directly: "i think u got virtuacam a lil twisted i intend on integrating it as in-runspace virtual camera and scrcpy like transport... like im actively integrating it into the source tree." He is hands-on building this himself, right now, in the tree - the CR documents direction, it does not prescribe an architecture that might conflict with live work. THE REAL REMAINING GAP, correctly framed: the broker/multiplexer/DirectPort-producer pattern already proven for LOCAL camera compositing extends to a scrcpy-like TRANSPORT - a phone (or another ss Agent peer, CRQ173) becomes a DirectPort producer feeding the SAME already-existing broker, over the wire (UDP courier, CRQ169) instead of only same-machine shared D3D11 handles. This is what actually replaces scrcpy - not a new broker concept, the SAME one, fed across a device boundary instead of only a process boundary. Standard RAG: the LLM is primary, an occasional vector lookup is a helper tool. Inverted: the embedding/similarity structure (FAISS - Meta's mature, GPU-accelerated ANN library, sub-millisecond search over billions of vectors via product quantization + inverted indexing) becomes the primary substrate a small model (e2b) composes/retrieves against, with generation shrunk to last-mile expression. This is the SAME thesis as Rung 4s e2b registry-hive, expressed at a different scale - the registry-hive is the durable per-concept store (Fence-stamped, entity-routed); FAISS is the FAST NEAREST-NEIGHBOR INDEX over that stores embeddings, letting retrieval happen at the speed the "wealth" demands once it is large. Do not reimplement FAISS - it is a solved, extremely optimized problem (SIMD, GPU kernels), unlike QNN/ONNX where owning the primitive was a sovereignty question. Wrap the real FAISS C++ library via P/Invoke; the RESULT set (matched vectors/handles) becomes VOM-native (a Region/Handle) even though the search kernel itself is FAISSs own code. Blocked on: the wealth itself - populate the index from e2bs own accumulating registry-hive (Rung 4) over normal operation, not a separate harvesting campaign, per Scotts stated position that training should not be necessary given how much capability already sits in freely available open weights - harvest/hoard embeddings, never retrain.

MOONSHOT BANKED - the two SGP&B-report components beyond latent-plan-mode (Rung 3b), from a research report Scott shared and said to bank ("u said it was sharp so bank it") without naming its working title. Two REAL, separable ideas worth building, distinct from the report's speculative hardware-texture-sampling parts (already correctly discarded as bullshit - no custom GPU kernels needed for any of this):
(1) LOAD-BEARING CONCEPT TRACKING (the report calls it a "Z-buffer" - depth-map metaphor, skip the metaphor, keep the mechanism): aggregate attention-entropy/variance per layer+head across a forward pass into one scalar "how persistent/load-bearing is this concept" score per position - grounded in real interpretability work (sparse autoencoders, attention as attractor patterns). USE: this score is exactly what should gate the KV-eviction distillery in Rung 4 - spend the distillery's compute on load-bearing concepts first, let genuinely transient ones fall out undistilled. Diffing this score between two states of the same context (before/after new info arrives) pinpoints WHERE the conceptual structure changed, cheaply, without re-reading the whole context.
(2) SPARSE CORRECTION / SEEK-AND-PATCH instead of full recompute: when new information arrives (a user correction, new context), use the diff from (1) to identify the SPECIFIC affected region and apply a small, targeted update there rather than replaying the whole context from scratch - the video-keyframe-plus-delta-frame analogy. This is the mechanism for handling mid-conversation corrections/errata cheaply once (1) exists to point at what needs patching.
(3) NOTED, NOT PRIORITIZED YET: the report's claim that a large model's prefill phase is embarrassingly parallel across multiple GPU dies is real and directly applicable to Scott's actual hardware (4x AMD Radeon Pro V340, per his v340l-windows-enablement research repo) - a big cognitive-prefill-only engine (Rung 3b's third phase) could split context ingestion across all four dies at HBM2 bandwidth speed, never touching the expensive serial decode path on that hardware at all. Summary: ONE KERNEL, N COURIERS - MCP serving on Windows. Scott 2026-07-01 verbatim: "surely there is a smart way to make sssd and ss.exe talk to each other using the windows registry when we are on windows ... make it a proper service that ss.exe can reach out to efficiently and say hi i am here ... like my directport discoverability system" + "we should only ever have a single sssd.exe right? a multiplexing service that handles all mcp serving on windows?" + "i will install it or we can make it prompt the user to install it always opt-in". RULING: the singleton is the KERNEL, not the shim. sssd.exe stays tiny and per-client (a stdio courier is per-client by nature; 4KB each is correct) but every shim rendezvouses to ONE resident ss kernel via a registry announce - HKCU\Software\Subsystem\Kernel = {pipe endpoint, PID, generation fence, binary hash} - announce/scan/connect, the DirectPort discoverability recipe verbatim. First shim finds no live kernel (PID-validated, stale key ignored) -> spawns + announces it; later shims Open the pipe and Register as peers; each client session is a VOM OWNER with its own runspace (Rs) inside the one kernel, so a wedged client is Terminate-d/cascade-killed without touching the others and disconnect reclaims exactly that owner. WHY: today N clients = N x ~230MB CoreCLR children with N PRIVATE VOMs - drivers cannot see each other (breaks CRQ168 awareness; Get-ChildItem vom:\Agent should show every connected driver LIVE), CRQ183 would need N copies of e2b instead of one resident her, CRQ177 would have N swap targets instead of one. Risky engines (DPX GPU decode) run as child producer processes owned by the kernel (the VirtuaCam broker/producer split) so a native fault cannot down every driver at once. SCM service install = boot-start convenience only, ALWAYS OPT-IN prompted, never silent (default-deny, Grant). Tonight's 0xffffffff: a stale relaunch during the 18:24 binary-swap window left a duplicate sssd/ss pair; Refresh fixed the client; this design removes the leak class.

EosLog.Body: POSTMORTEM (evidence: %APPDATA%\Claude\logs\mcp-server-Subsystem.log) + RUNG 1 SHIPPED (d7196a9). Tonight's two flaps, exactly: (1) the red "exit status 0xffffffff / 5 tools" panel = a client relaunch racing the 18:24 binary-swap window (rename-then-copy leaves a ~1s gap with no ss.exe; launch in the gap dies -1 and the client caches the error); at 18:34:22 it relaunched clean on the new exe = the green 6-tool panel. (2) the 19:12:31 "Server transport closed unexpectedly / Server disconnected" = Fable killing pid 21460/10780 believing the pair orphaned - it was the desktop app's LIVE server; nothing on the box recorded which server serves which client. A third latent class found by inspection: stdout IS the JSON-RPC wire and any stray console write (log sink, runspace [Console]::WriteLine) would poison it mid-stream. RUNG 1 (shipped, gate GREEN 573/0): Mcp protocol mode parks the rpc writer and reroutes Console.Out to stderr (wire cannot be poisoned - proven by an in-runspace poison probe in the new receipt test.windows.mcp-stdout-purity.ps1, 10/10 asserts); lifecycle breadcrumbs on stderr so the client log carries every future flap's cause; shutdown reclaim guarded so clean disconnect never paints as a crash; and the first announce slice - HKCU\Software\Subsystem\Mcp\<pid> = {Exe, StartedUtc, ExeWriteUtc}, removed on clean exit - ownership readable before anyone kills anything. PATH TO 99.9: RUNG 2 = CRQ177 (Sonnet, claimed target = the kernel): in-situ slot swap kills the binary-swap race class - no more rename/copy gap, one .prev max. RUNG 3 = this CRQ's kernel: one resident VOM all sssd shims rendezvous to via the announce (generation fence bumps on swap; shims survive it); client flaps then NEVER touch the kernel and kernel swaps never touch clients. RUNG 4 = receipt test.rs.mcp-reliability.ps1: N connect/disconnect cycles + a swap under load, zero stream corruption, exit 0 every time. Deployed ss.exe swapped to the rung-1 build 19:18:46 - running servers keep the old image until their client reconnects; refresh at leisure.

Summary: DPX AS CHIMERA - the runtime thesis, settled. Scott 2026-07-01 verbatim: "can dpx be more than onnxruntime? can it be a chimera of all the best parts of ggml/qnn/trt even?". The fight DPX wins is NOT the kernel race against ORT - it is the substrate race nobody else is running: (1) model.db is queryable/mutable TRUTH (graph=rows, tensors=BLOB, CRQ144/158/162) where every other runtime has an opaque artifact; (2) memory is VOM-owned and deterministic (DpxTensor q4 off the GC, quota, cascade-kill, CRQ164); (3) the data plane IS DirectPort - a tensor is a fenced shareable region, so cross-process/cross-device placement is a property of the type, not a feature bolted on; (4) sovereign and auditable end to end (trusting-trust, CRQ180). ORGAN THEFTS, in order: FROM GGML - the q4 SIMD dot-kernel discipline (AVX2/NEON) for the CPU hot loop; the 0.5 tok/s decode is a kernel-quality gap, not an architecture gap. FROM TRT - ahead-of-time cooked plans: fused op chains + chosen tactics persisted INTO model.db as rows (a plans table beside the tensors - the db makes TRT's engine-blob pattern natural, and the proven model.db->HTP context-binary (CRQ158) already IS this pattern for the NPU; extend it to DXIL/SPIR-V for the GPU). FROM QNN - the Hexagon door Scott personally opened (own blob format, HMX swizzle decoded); per-op CPU/GPU/NPU placement rides the same cooked-plan rows. ORT - stays OUTSIDE as the offline parity oracle (CRQ121 doctrine), demoted from runtime to referee; every kernel tournament and cooked plan must beat/match the oracle numerically in its receipt. KERNEL TOURNAMENT (the acquisition mechanism): Scott grabbed remix_-spinnerevolve (Downloads) - an LLM-mutation evolutionary loop (progenitor code -> model mutates -> render -> fitness -> select). Same primitive over kernels: mutate gemm.hlsl/gemm.comp variants (tile/workgroup/unroll), run each against a fixed workload on the REAL adapter, fitness = measured ms + oracle parity, winner cooked into model.db per (op-shape, device). e2b/Gemini is the mutator, exactly as in the grabbed app. TRT tactic selection, rebuilt as the shader tournament.

EosLog.Body: SHARPENED - the chimera is RECIPE THEFT, never CODE theft. Scott 2026-07-01 verbatim: "not trying to thieve what is the proper way to build dpx into something greater than the sum of its parts and thank ggml for giving us the recipes we can use to accelerate" + "i refuse to import libraries". LAW (the runtime twin of CRQ144 "every compile dep must defend its own existence"): DPX imports ZERO inference libraries - not ggml, not llama.cpp, not QNN's runtime as a linked dep, not ORT. What we take is the RECIPE: the algorithm, the memory layout, the tile math, the swizzle formula - reimplemented as OUR OWN code (C VOM / HLSL / SPIR-V / our own Hexagon blobs), each carrying a cited breadcrumb to the open work that taught it (exactly as the receipts already do: hmx-swizzle-RECEIPT.md credits haozixu/llama.cpp-npu + htp-ops-lib by file and function; qnn-htp-RECEIPT.md credits the QnnGraph API path). Attribution is the mechanism, not an afterthought - thank the source in the code comment and the receipt, link nothing. THE FOUR-PART METHOD to build greater-than-the-sum: (1) RECIPE, not binary - port the technique, cite the teacher; ggml gave the q4 dot-kernel and flash-attention tiling recipes, haozixu gave the HMX layout, we WRITE them. (2) ORACLE DISCIPLINE - ggml/ORT stay OUTSIDE as numerical referees; every DPX kernel must match the oracle within tolerance in its receipt (this is how you inherit their correctness without their dependency). (3) COOKED PLANS AS ROWS - the winning kernel per (op-shape, device) is persisted into model.db beside the tensors (TRT's engine-blob pattern, made natural by the db); the shader tournament (spinnerevolve primitive) is the selection mechanism. (4) THE UNIFICATION THE DONORS CANNOT DO - model.db as queryable truth, VOM-owned deterministic memory, DirectPort as the data plane so a tensor is a shareable fenced region, per-op CPU/GPU/NPU placement over ONE primitive. The donors shipped libraries a process LINKS; DPX is a substrate workloads LIVE IN. That gap - sovereignty + one primitive at every scale - is the "greater than the sum", and it is only reachable BECAUSE we refuse to import. NOVELTY, honestly (web-checked 2026-07-01, and the receipts say so themselves): the HMX swizzle was opened by haozixu (llama.cpp-npu, htp-ops-lib), NOT first-invented here; reverse-engineering QAIRT is an active field (arxiv 2509.23324, datavorous QAIRT writeup). What is distinctive here is the SOVEREIGN IN-PROCESS INTEGRATION - converter-free/python-free on-device context-binary generation (Route A) + a pure-PowerShell swizzle proof (Route C) wired into a self-hosting model.db substrate - not the format crack. Claim the integration, credit the cartographers.

BANKED (Scott 2026-07-01, closing the provenance discussion): the recipe-not-code doctrine + the honest novelty framing above are settled - stop re-litigating, build. Distinctive claim = the sovereign in-process integration (converter-free/python-free on-device Route A + pure-PS swizzle Route C wired into model.db); the HMX layout crack is haozixu's, credited in the receipts. Proceed to real work: DPX decode-profile receipt -> name the hot op -> port the ONE ggml recipe (q4 dot-kernel) as our own C-VOM kernel validated against the oracle. No more discussion of firsts/repos - the git history + hash-anchored receipts ARE the provenance.

STEP 1 DONE (Sonnet 5, c11ed3c) - THE HOT OP IS NAMED, EMPIRICALLY. Dp.Profile/Dp.Prof existed as a dead hook (Scott-adjacent finding: it double-Dispatched every node when enabled, silently 2x-ing any profile run - fixed, one-line). Wired --profile into ss dpx-generate; ran against the REAL gemma4-e2b-onnx-decoder-q4.db (S:\modeldb, 1.87GB) for 16 tokens: MatMulNBits = 189.9s of 194.1s = 97.8% of decode time, 3872 calls. Not a guess anymore.

THE PORT, SCOPED (recipe theft per CRQ190 doctrine - cite, reimplement, never link): current MatMulNBits (Dp.cs:818-854) is a fully scalar triple-nested loop (per output-row x per M-row x per k-in-block: unpack one nibble, multiply by one fp32 activation, accumulate) - zero SIMD, zero threading beyond the outer Parallel.For(N).

Pulled ggml's AVX2 q4_0 dot-kernel recipe (ggml-org/llama.cpp, ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c, ggml_vec_dot_q4_0_q8_0) and diffed it against our actual format:
- ggml q4_0: SYMMETRIC, block=32, dequant = (nibble - 8) * fp16_scale, no separate zero-point tensor, activations REQUANTIZED to int8 (block_q8_0) so the dot is int8xint8 via _mm256_maddubs_epi16 + _mm256_madd_epi16, THEN scaled by (d_weight*d_activation) via one _mm256_fmadd_ps, horizontal-summed.
- our MatMulNBits (com.microsoft contrib op): block=32, UNSIGNED 4-bit, dequant = (nibble - zp) * scale where zp is an EXPLICIT per-block nibble-packed tensor (defaults to 8 = 2^(bits-1) when absent). KEY FINDING: when the zp tensor is absent, our formula is IDENTICAL to ggmls (same implicit center, same block size) - the port is a direct application, not an adaptation, for that case. When zp IS present it generalizes to a per-block broadcast subtract instead of a compile-time constant 8.
- SECOND KEY DIFFERENCE: our activations stay fp32 the whole time (no int8 requantization) - so the target port is ggmls SIMPLER f32-activation dot-with-dequant shape, not the dual-quant int8xint8 path: unpack 8 nibbles/iter -> widen to int32 -> cvt to float -> subtract zp (per-block scalar or vector broadcast) -> _mm256_loadu_ps 8 activations -> _mm256_fmadd_ps -> accumulate -> multiply by block scale once per block -> horizontal sum. Smaller lift than the full ggml kernel - no activation quantization step needed.

NEXT: port that loop as OUR OWN C-VOM AVX2 kernel (System.Runtime.Intrinsics.X86 or a native VOM kernel per CRQ190's C-ABI seam), validated against the current scalar path as the numerical oracle (CRQ121 doctrine) within fp32 tolerance, receipted with a before/after ms/call number replacing todays 190s/16-token baseline. What was NOT verified and remains unproven: whether the NIBBLE BYTE-PACKING ORDER also matches (same formula + transposed layout = silent garbage). Summary: ONE MODEL, ONE DB - consolidate the gemma4-e2b face files into a single gemma4-e2b.db. Scott 2026-07-01 verbatim: "shouldnt we consolidate those separate db files into a single gemma4-e2b-onnx.db?". Today S:\modeldb carries embed-q4 (1.76GB) + decoder-q4 (1.87GB) + vision-fp16 + audio-fp16 as separate dbs plus a loose gemma-4-e2b.spm. Consolidate: one db, FACES as named graphs in rows (embed/decoder/vision/audio), the .spm tokenizer as a blob table (self-describing model - no loose sidecar), a manifest table (hashes, quant, provenance), per-tensor format columns as today. The reason is not tidiness: ROWS, not files, are the streaming unit - the federated mesh (CRQ173) and the UDP courier (CRQ169) pull tensors/experts selectively over DirectPort, so file boundaries stop mattering the moment the faces share one db; and cooked plans (chimera CRQ) land beside the tensors they compile. DEADPOOL FLAG (Scott decides): gemma4-e2b-litert.db (2.56GB) is the retired LiteRT lane (CRQ170) - delete once ONNX-lane parity is receipted.

EosLog.Body: MULTIMODAL FACE SEPARATION - the fp16/q4 seam is a real design decision, not an accident to inherit. Confirmed on disk: S:\modeldb carries decoder-q4 (1.87GB) + embed-q4 (1.76GB) alongside vision-fp16 (338MB) + audio-fp16 (591MB) - four SEPARATE ONNX exports today, the exact files CRQ191 (one model, one db) proposes consolidating as named-graph faces. Two things the consolidation must decide explicitly, not inherit from however the ONNX export happened to shape it: (1) HOT-OP SCOPE IS PER-FACE - the CRQ190 step-1 receipt (MatMulNBits 97.8% of decode time) is DECODER-ONLY; vision/audio are fp16 and near-certainly Conv/attention-dominated (general Gemma 3n architecture: a vision tower + USM-style audio encoder producing embeddings), meaning the kernel tournament needs a SEPARATE profiling pass per face before claiming a hot op for vision or audio - do not assume the decoder finding generalizes. (2) THE FUSION-POINT PRECISION SEAM - multimodal embeddings arrive fp16, the decoder consumes its own token embeddings via GatherBlockQuantized (q4). Whether fused multimodal tokens get requantized to match or the decoder stays mixed-precision at that boundary needs a stated decision in the CRQ191 consolidation, not silent inheritance. UPSIDE: multimodality is the natural first candidate for cross-device FACE splitting in the federated mesh (CRQ173/185) - a phone runs its vision encoder locally where the camera already is, and only the resulting embedding tensor (much smaller than raw frames) crosses DirectPort to wherever the decoder runs. The clearest concrete case yet for "a tensor is a shareable fenced region, placement is a property of the type."

Summary: 16 KB PAGE ALIGNMENT — Samsung S23 (Android 16) 'Android App Compatibility' dialog: ELF alignment check failed, our bundled native libs are not 16 KB aligned. Transcribed verbatim from on-device screenshot 2026-07-03 (scratchpad/elf_err.png): 'This app isn't 16 KB compatible. ELF alignment check failed. Please follow the steps on https://developer.android.com/16kb-page-size. The following libraries are not 16 KB aligned: lib/arm64-v8a/libSystem.Native.so : Unknown error; lib/arm64-v8a/libxamarin-app.so : Unknown error; lib/arm64-v8a/libcoreclr.so : Unknown error; lib/arm64-v8a/libQnnHtp.so : Unknown error; lib/arm64-v8a/libSystem.Security.Cryptography.Native.Android.so : Unknown error; lib/arm64-v8a/libSystem.Globalization.Native.so : Unknown [truncated].' Two lib families implicated: (1) the .NET/CoreCLR runtime pack (libcoreclr.so, libSystem.Native.so, libxamarin-app.so, libSystem.*.Native.so) and (2) the QUALCOMM prebuilts we bundle (libQnnHtp.so — and by extension the rest of the QAIRT stack + our disguised libqnnworker.so).

EosLog.Body: SEVERITY / BLAST RADIUS (measured on-device, not assumed): the S23 (RFCWA0CE47F, SM8550) is CURRENTLY running 4 KB pages (getconf PAGE_SIZE = 4096), so THIS dialog is ADVISORY — the app loads and runs (pid alive, ProjectionServer listening on 8080), the misaligned libs still dlopen on a 4 KB kernel. So 16 KB alignment is NOT what is blocking the S23 QNN-worker bring-up right now (that is a separate forward/HTTP issue). BUT it is a real, dated blocker for two reasons: (1) FATAL on any 16 KB-page device — Android 16 devices can ship/toggle 16 KB pages, and a misaligned lib fails to mmap (dlopen 'CANNOT LINK') there, which would harden this warning into a crash; (2) Google Play MANDATES 16 KB compatibility for apps targeting Android 15+ submitted/updated after 2025-11-01. FIX DIRECTION, per implicated family: (A) .NET runtime libs (libcoreclr/libSystem.Native/libxamarin-app/libSystem.*.Native) come from the .NET Android runtime pack — need a .NET SDK/workload build that emits 16 KB-aligned runtime .so (the toolchain's linker must pass -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384; confirm the pinned dotnet on S:\bin\dotnet produces aligned output or bump the Android workload), NOT something we can zipalign after the fact for correctness of the segment alignment. (B) The QAIRT prebuilts (libQnnHtp.so et al.) ship 4 KB-aligned from Qualcomm's SDK — re-link/re-align them (or pull a newer QAIRT that ships 16 KB-aligned), and REBUILD our disguised worker binary libqnnworker.so (the mm_qnn ELF) with -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384. (C) Verify end-state with the NDK check: alignment must be 0x4000 on every PT_LOAD across every lib/arm64-v8a/*.so, and re-test on a device forced to 16 KB pages. Cross-refs: this rode in on the NPU-on-S23 bring-up (DpxQnnWorker child-process path); the S23 grants untrusted_app the DSP node (unlike the razr's Motorola sepolicy), so the S23 IS the target device for our-own-model NPU and MUST be 16 KB-clean. Screenshot saved at scratchpad/elf_err.png (session cf00a11b).
